headline: Privacy is control over your personal information—deciding what to share and with whom
universal_truth: What you share shapes how you're seen; control over information is control over identity
fun_facts: The average person is tracked by over 100 companies without their knowledge
Once information is shared digitally, you lose control of it forever
Privacy concerns date back to ancient times—it's not just a modern issue
discussion_questions: What information do you share freely that might deserve more protection?
How do you decide what's appropriate to share?
What have you shared that you wish you hadn't?

hook.title: Welcome
hook.script: Your thoughts, your history, your preferences—these are yours. You get to decide who knows what. Privacy isn't about hiding wrongdoing; it's about controlling the narrative of who you are.

options.text: I want to learn something new
options.response: Perfect. Curiosity is the first step to understanding. Let's explore this together.
That curiosity is exactly what we need. Let's dive in and discover something amazing.

cliff.title: The Question
cliff.script: Some say 'if you have nothing to hide, you have nothing to fear.' But privacy matters even for the innocent. Why?

options.text: Privacy enables autonomy—controlling what's known about you is controlling how you're perceived and treated; without privacy, you lose power over your own identity and choices
options.response: Yes. Information is power. Who knows what about you affects what opportunities you get, how you're judged, what's marketed to you. Privacy is self-determination.
Secrets are part of it, but privacy is broader—it's about control, not necessarily concealment...

q1.title: Context Matters
q1.script: What's appropriate to share depends on context. Something fine to tell a doctor might not be fine on social media. Privacy is context-appropriate sharing, not universal secrecy.
q1.prompt: What's your first impression of "Context Matters"?

options.text: This confirms what I already knew
options.response: Great foundation! Now let's build on that knowledge with something you might not expect...
Perfect starting point! This insight will connect to even more surprising facts ahead.

q2.title: Irreversibility
q2.script: Digital sharing is often irreversible. Once out, information can spread beyond control. Consider permanence before sharing—what feels okay now might not later.
q2.prompt: How does this connect to what you already know?

options.response: Exactly. These connections are how knowledge becomes understanding.

options.text: I need to think about this more
options.response: That's a good instinct. Deep understanding takes time. The next fact will help clarify.

q3.title: Active Choice
q3.script: Privacy requires active decisions. Default settings often share more than you'd choose. Actively review what you're sharing and with whom. Don't let default determine disclosure.
q3.prompt: What surprises you most about this?

options.text: I never thought about it this way
options.response: That shift in perspective is exactly the point. New angles reveal new truths.
That's learning in action. When understanding shifts, you're really getting it.

wisdom.title: Today's Wisdom
wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: What you share shapes how you're seen. Control over information is control over identity. Protect your privacy deliberately.
wisdom.prompt: What resonates most with you today?

options.response: That central truth will stay with you. Let it guide your thinking.
Application is where knowledge becomes wisdom. That's the real learning.

outro.title: See You Tomorrow
outro.script: That's Day 322. Tomorrow, we'll explore who you are—identity. Until then, consider what you're sharing and whether it's by choice.
outro.prompt: Before you go—what will you take from today?

options.response: Reflection deepens learning. Let these ideas simmer in your mind.
Teaching others is the best way to learn. You've already begun the ripple.

growTrack.title: Privacy Audit - What Are You Sharing?
growTrack.learning_objective: Assess and adjust personal information sharing
growTrack.activity: Review what information you've shared publicly—on social media, in conversations, through apps. Is it what you'd choose to share? What deserves more protection? Make one adjustment to improve your privacy.
